title: Test: subtitles, Kachi, voice
description:
North Korea banned a tiny chocolate snack from South Korea. Then 10,000 of them flew over the border on balloons. I'm Kachi, and this is the wild true story of Choco Pie: born on a trip to Georgia, USA, traded like money in Korea's army, a tea-time legend in Russia, an offering on Vietnamese altars, and a black-market treasure in the North.

Chapters
{chapters}

Where did you eat your first Choco Pie? Tell me in the comments.

lines: This tiny snack got banned in North Korea.
Not a weapon. Not a phone. A snack.
Hi! I'm Kachi, the little magpie who brings you the weirdest true stories from Korea.
Today's star is Orion's Choco Pie. It costs less than a coffee, sits in every convenience store here,
and somehow lived a wilder life than most people.
Meet the Orion Choco Pie. Two soft cakes, a marshmallow middle, and a chocolate coat.
Simple, right? Wait till you see where it's been.
And here's the joke every Korean guy knows.
On Sundays, religious services on base hand out free snacks.
So suddenly, a lot of soldiers become very, very spiritual.
Church in the morning, temple after lunch, whoever has the better snacks.

pops.text: Wearing the stuff from all three religions at once was basically the rule.
pops.orig: 세 종교에서 준거 다 차고다니는게 국룰이였는데

pops.text: I wandered around and finally settled at the temple that gave out fruit lol
pops.orig: 이곳저곳 떠돌다 결국 과일 주는 절에 정착했던 기억ㅋㅋㅋㅋ

lines: And with a glass of hot tea at the end of the day? Chef's kiss.
Then, around 2000, a TV ad made it legendary.
A little boy asks: Mom, where's the Choco Pie?
Except he mumbles it so badly, a whole generation of Russians heard something like: go give the duck a bath.

pops.text: My whole childhood I wanted to know what he says. Turns out it's "Where's the Choco Pie?" I thought it was "pichkupai" or "dichkupai".
pops.orig: Всё детство мечтал узнать что он говорит, оказывается "Где чокопай?"
